title: A Summer for the Bakery
premise: Lior Fairweather, a widowed single parent keeping the harbor town's only bookshop afloat, joins the library's anonymous summer pen-pal program to please his daughter — only to be matched, by a clerical error neither can undo, with his bitterest rival: Marguerite Voss, whose family's bakery empire is buying up the waterfront and threatening his lease. Writing under assumed names, they fall for the strangers on paper while clashing openly in person, each unaware the other knows. When Marguerite discovers the truth and realizes her family's development deal will raze the bookshop block, she must defy her father's corrupt machine — and Lior must choose between a lucrative corporate offer that would secure his daughter's future and the woman who finally sees him whole. They confess everything at the last ferry of the season, she publicly breaks the deal, and the epilogue-adjacent final chapters find the bakery and bookshop sharing one rebuilt storefront — and one family.
about_author: Kestrel Eastwick is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes love stories set in places where everyone knows your overdue fines. She lives near the coast with her family and a sourdough starter older than her marriage.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Opening the bookshop on the first warm morning of June, Lior counts a register that won't survive August and fields his daughter Poppy's plea to join the library's anonymous pen-pal program. He agrees mostly to make her stop worrying about him. Beat: a man teaching his heart to stay closed, and almost succeeding.

chapters.title: Flour in the Air
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite runs Voss Bakery with her father's iron rules and no recipes of her own. He announces the waterfront acquisition — including the bookshop block — and orders her to charm the town into compliance. She signs her name to a pen-pal card at the library to feel like someone else. Beat: complicity dressed as duty.

chapters.title: A Clerical Error
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The library's volunteer coordinator, flustered by a spilled coffee, mismatches the anonymous letters. Lior receives his first pen-pal letter and recognizes the handwriting from a signed complaint filed against his shop — Marguerite Voss. He nearly reports the error, then pockets the letter instead. Beat: curiosity as the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite realizes her pen pal is Fairweather when he quotes her father's lease language back at her, disguised as small talk. Furious, she decides to write anyway — to interrogate the enemy. Their letters turn into a chess game of veiled insults and accidental honesty. Beat: hostility sharpening into attention.

chapters.title: Poppy's Map
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Poppy, ten and relentless, draws a map of every business her father might lose and asks which one will be hers. Lior lies that the shop is safe, then takes a call from a corporate bookstore chain offering a lifeline with strings. Beat: the cost of protection — and what it teaches a child.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Supper
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The town's midsummer potluck forces the rivals into the same room. They spar publicly over the development, but Marguerite catches Lior giving his dessert to a hungry kid and recognizes the man from the letters. She says nothing. Beat: the first moment the mask slips in daylight.

chapters.title: What the Letters Knew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A letter arrives that is too tender to be strategy — Marguerite writes about her mother's lost recipes and a childhood spent measuring love in proofing times. Lior, shaken, writes back something true for the first time. Beat: intimacy arriving through a side door neither guarded.

chapters.title: The Lease Clause
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Digging through her father's files to protect her own bakery's independence, Marguerite finds the clause that lets Voss Holdings terminate the bookshop's lease early. She photographs it, then hides it — loyalty and conscience at war. Beat: complicity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Rain on the Promenade
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A storm strands Lior and Marguerite under the same awning after a council meeting. Soaked, exhausted, they argue about the waterfront and accidentally tell the truth: neither chose the war they're fighting. They part without touching. Beat: the almost, and the ache of it.

chapters.title: The Chain's Offer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The corporate chain sweetens its offer: a management salary, Poppy's tuition, security. Lior drafts an acceptance letter and leaves it unsigned on the counter for three days. Poppy finds it and, without a word, adds her map to the pile. Beat: love as an unpaid debt he cannot stop trying to service.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite secretly recreates her mother's cardamom loaf from a water-stained recipe card, and for the first time bakes something that is hers. Her father catches her and calls it a distraction. That night she mails a letter admitting she is afraid of becoming him. Beat: the self surfacing through craft.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Sorting donations, Lior finds a bakery flyer with Marguerite's handwriting and matches it, line by line, to his pen pal. The knowledge lands like a fall: the tenderness was real, and so was the enemy. He stops answering. Beat: betrayal felt most sharply where trust had grown.

chapters.title: The Unanswered Letter
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Three letters go unanswered. Marguerite, wounded and suspicious, concludes her pen pal discovered her identity and was playing her all along. She throws herself into her father's campaign, and the town notices her going cold. Beat: hurt weaponized into armor.

chapters.title: Public Hearing
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The zoning hearing on the waterfront demolition. Lior testifies for the bookshop; Marguerite, seated beside her father, must sit silent as the deal advances. Their eyes meet once across the chamber. Poppy, in the audience, sees her father lose and understands the lie. Beat: public defeat, private devastation.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite finds her father shredding documents ahead of an ethics inquiry and realizes the development was never about the bakery — it's a laundering scheme, and her name is on the filings. She copies the lease clause and the ledger pages. Beat: fear transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior signs the chain's acceptance — then learns Marguerite has been quietly paying the shop's back rent anonymously since June, routed through the library. The pen pal and the enemy collapse into one person who was protecting him all along. The last ferry of the season leaves Saturday. Beat: everything he believed inverted in one receipt.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Ovens
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Lior comes to the bakery at closing. No letters, no aliases — just the raw truth: anger, gratitude, and the question of whether anything between them was real. Marguerite shows him the ledger pages and asks for one day to end it properly. Beat: honesty as the only viable currency left.

chapters.title: The Father's House
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite confronts her father with the evidence and demands he withdraw the acquisition. He threatens to disown her and ruin her name with the business. She walks out with her mother's recipe cards and nothing else. Beat: the found family beginning where the blood family ends.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Saturday. Lior tears up the chain contract at the dock as Marguerite arrives, breathless, holding the withdrawal notice and the evidence for the press. On the ferry deck, in front of Poppy and half the town, they say the true names of everything they feel. Beat: the choice made — person over security, presence over containment.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The ethics inquiry and the council revote. Marguerite testifies against her own family's company; Lior and the town's small business owners stand with her. The waterfront block is designated a heritage district. Her father exits the courtroom without looking back. Beat: power confronted publicly, and broken.

chapters.title: Shared Storefront
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Autumn. The bookshop and bakery knock through the wall between them — one door, two names on the glass. Poppy does homework at the corner table; Marguerite's cardamom loaf sells out by ten. Lior still writes letters, but now he hands them over in person. Beat: the quiet reward after the storm.

chapters.title: A Summer, Kept
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, closing. One year later, the library launches a new pen-pal season. Lior and Marguerite, now co-signing one card, write the program's opening letter to strangers: tell the truth early, and forgive the clerical errors. Poppy pins her old map to the wall, every shop still standing. Beat: memory honored, family chosen, the heart retrained at last.
